questions.question: Why does the code warm and synchronize before entering the trace, then measure a separate unprofiled loop?
options: Warmup removes all host activity, so the trace contains only accelerator instructions

The fixed-signature warmup moves initial compilation out of the captured window; the trace still records whatever host, device, synchronization and profiler events occur, while the unprofiled loop supplies a separate wall-time measurement
A matrix dot automatically inserts a cross-device collective, which the profiler needs to show
questions.explanation: The synchronized warmup prepares the tested signature before tracing. The captured function is one fixed-input dot and includes no collective, so it cannot support a communication claim. Trace event durations may nest or overlap and include runtime/profiler activity. The separate unprofiled measurement includes host dispatch and synchronization; it is not a device-only latency.
optionFeedback: Warmup excludes the first invocation from the trace but does not remove host dispatch, synchronization, other compilation events, or profiler overhead from captured work.

The synchronized warmup prepares the tested signature before tracing. The captured function is one fixed-input dot and includes no collective, so it cannot support a communication claim. Trace event durations may nest or overlap and include runtime/profiler activity. The separate unprofiled measurement includes host dispatch and synchronization; it is not a device-only latency.
A dot call on one array does not imply a distributed collective. Communication appears only if the actual workload and trace contain such operations.
